title: Brill–Noether theory and gonality of finite graphs
abstract: Formalizes Brill–Noether existence through genus five, chains of marked banana graphs and loops, the treewidth lower bound for gonality, and a tricycle example whose gonality drops under regular subdivision. Includes divisor and transmission infrastructure and the Demazure-product support used by vertex gluing.

informal.Highlights.brill_noether_existence_throu: Every finite connected loopless multigraph of genus g at most five has, for integers r and d, a divisor of degree d and rank at least r whenever (r + 1) * (g - d + r) ≤ g.
informal.Highlights.treewidth_le_gonality: On a finite connected loopless multigraph, for every natural number k, any degree-k divisor of rank at least one bounds the treewidth by k; this is the witness formulation of the treewidth lower bound for divisorial gonality.
informal.Highlights.gonality_drops_under_regular_: There is a graph whose divisorial gonality strictly decreases under a regular subdivision.
